what: The score combines exact insertion distance with route-versus-unassigned geometric affinity, a depot-radius reward, residual-capacity packing, and a one-step spatial continuation check restricted to customers that would still fit. Position selection is driven by insertion delta; the remaining terms prioritize route membership. Runtime is O(len(current route) + len(unassigned)) per call with O(1) extra space.
why: Cheapest insertion alone can absorb depot-near customers too early and mix spatial clusters. The affinity contrast favors customers whose natural neighbor is already on the route, while the radial reward encourages sharing costly depot excursions. Capacity terms address both heterogeneous demands and premature route closure, as seen in instances ranging from one dominant demand to many moderate demands. The continuation term keeps geographically close, capacity-compatible successors available. Coefficients are conservative hand-designed tradeoffs, not empirically validated guarantees; the one-customer capacity lookahead cannot detect subset-sum packing opportunities, and geometric clustering may be less helpful on irregular or non-Euclidean demand layouts.
